name: גִּדְעֹנִי
summary: A man of Benjamin in the wilderness, known only as the father of Abidan, the prince of Benjamin at the numbering, at the offerings for the altar, and over Benjamin’s host when the camps set out from Sinai (Num 1:11; 7:60; 10:24). The name is the root of גָּדַע, “hew down, cut off”, with the endings ־וֹן and ־ִי, the same stem as Gideon’s name (Judges 6–8) with a further ־ִי; scripture does not explain the name, so “hewer” rests on the verb’s use.

evidence.note: “And over the host of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, Abidan son of גִּדְעוֹנִי”, spelled here with the full ו.
Abidan son of Gideoni brings Benjamin’s offering on the ninth day (and 7:65).
The root’s verb: “their Asherahs you shall hew down (תְּגַדֵּעוּן)”.
גְּדוּעִים, “hewn down”, of the high of stature felled like trees.
גִּדְעוֹן, Gideon: the same stem without the final ־ִי.

note: The force of the endings is not settled: ־וֹן may make a noun of the verb (“hewing” or “hewer”) and ־ִי may be the first-person suffix (“my hewer”) or the ending of a name of descent; “hewer” is given as the plain reading. Gideoni lived long before the judge Gideon, so his name is not taken from Gideon’s. The verb is also used of Benjamin itself, “one tribe hewn off from Israel” (Jdg 21:6), but nothing ties that to his name. The name occurs at Num 1:11; 2:22; 7:60, 65; 10:24.
